query: Generate positive, negative, and boundary test cases for Booking.com flight search based on the available PRD and screenshots.

use_cases.use_case_title: One-way and round-trip flight search with filters
use_cases.goal: Verify that users can successfully perform one-way and round-trip flight searches and refine results using core filters (stops, airlines, times, duration) with correct, fast, and consistent behavior.
preconditions: User can access Booking.com Flights page via web.
System is integrated with airline and GDS providers and can return real-time availability and pricing.
Localization for INR currency is available for the India locale.
Flight Filters feature is enabled on the flight results page.
steps: Navigate to Booking.com and select the Flights tab.
Select trip type as Round-trip.
Enter origin as MAA (Chennai International Airport).
Enter destination as London (All airports).
Select departure date as a valid future date (e.g., 2026-01-24).
Select return date as a valid future date after the departure date (e.g., 2026-01-31).
Select Travelers as 1 adult and cabin class as Economy.
Click the Search button.
Observe that the flight results page loads with default filters applied (e.g., Stops = Any).
Verify that the number of results and minimum price are displayed for each stops option (Any, Direct only, 1 stop max).
Apply the 'Direct only' filter and observe that results update dynamically.
Change the stops filter to '1 stop max' and observe that results update dynamically.
Open the Airlines filter and select one or more airlines (e.g., Etihad Airways, Air India).
Apply a departure time bucket (e.g., 6:00 AM–11:59 AM) for the departing flight.
Apply an arrival time bucket (e.g., 6:00 AM–11:59 AM) for the arrival to destination.
Set the maximum travel time (duration) to a valid value (e.g., 40 hours).
Observe that results update within the specified performance requirement after each filter change.
Switch trip type to One-way, keep the same origin and destination, select only a departure date, and repeat the search.
Verify that filters behave consistently for the One-way search and that results are shown with updated counts and prices.
expected_results: After clicking Search, the system returns flight options for the selected origin, destination, dates, passengers, and class, with initial results displayed within 3 seconds.
The results page shows a Filters section with Stops, Airlines, Flight times (departing and arrival), and Duration (maximum travel time).
The Stops filter displays options such as Any, Direct only, and 1 stop max, each with a result count and a 'From' price in INR.
When 'Direct only' is selected, only direct flights are shown, and the result count matches the count displayed in the filter.
When '1 stop max' is selected, only flights with at most one stop are shown, and the result count matches the count displayed in the filter.
When specific airlines are selected, only flights operated by those airlines appear in the results.
When a departure time bucket is selected, all displayed flights have departure times within the selected time range.
When an arrival time bucket is selected, all displayed flights have arrival times within the selected time range.
When maximum travel time is set (e.g., 40 hours), all displayed flights have total duration less than or equal to the specified maximum.
Each filter change triggers a dynamic update of the results, and the update completes within 500 ms.
The filter logic and behavior are consistent between Round-trip and One-way searches.
Currency is displayed as INR for prices when searching from the India locale.
The system maintains availability and pricing consistency with the underlying airline/GDS providers for the displayed results.
negative_cases: Attempt a Round-trip search with the return date earlier than the departure date and verify that the system prevents the search or shows a clear error (invalid date range).
Attempt a search with an invalid or non-existent airport code for origin or destination and verify that the system does not proceed to results and provides appropriate feedback.

Perform a valid search and then apply a combination of filters (e.g., specific airline + strict time buckets + very low maximum duration) that results in zero matching flights; verify that the system displays a clear 'no results' state rather than an error.

Simulate airline data missing for some fares (e.g., airline name not returned) and verify that the system still displays the fare gracefully or clearly indicates missing airline information without breaking the filters.
Simulate an airline API timeout during search and verify that the system handles it gracefully (e.g., partial results or error message) without crashing and without infinite loading.

Simulate a price change between search and booking (e.g., user sees a price in the results, then proceeds to the next step where the price has changed) and verify that the system informs the user of the updated price instead of silently using stale pricing.

Apply conflicting filter combinations (e.g., selecting an airline that does not operate direct flights while 'Direct only' is selected) and verify that the system either shows zero results with a clear message or adjusts filters in a predictable way, without inconsistent or incorrect results.
Change language or currency settings to a locale not supported by the flight search localization and verify that the system falls back gracefully without corrupting price display.
Attempt to perform a search with zero passengers (if allowed by UI interactions) and verify that the system prevents the search or shows an appropriate error.

Rapidly toggle multiple filters (stops, airlines, time buckets, duration) in quick succession and verify that the UI does not freeze, does not show inconsistent results, and handles overlapping requests gracefully.
boundary_cases: Use the earliest possible selectable departure date (e.g., today or the minimum future date allowed by the date picker) and verify that search and filters work correctly.
Use the latest possible selectable departure date (maximum date allowed by the date picker) and verify that search and filters work correctly.

Set the maximum travel time (duration) to its minimum allowed value (e.g., 0 or the smallest positive duration allowed) and verify that only flights meeting that strict duration are shown or that a clear 'no results' state appears if none match.

Set the maximum travel time (duration) to its maximum allowed value (e.g., 40 hours as shown in the UI) and verify that all flights with duration less than or equal to that value are eligible to appear.
Select all available airlines in the Airlines filter and verify that the results set is equivalent to having no airline filter applied (subject to other filters).
Select exactly one airline in the Airlines filter and verify that all displayed flights belong to that airline and that counts in the filter match the number of results.
Apply a departure time bucket that starts at 12:00 AM and ends at 5:59 AM and verify that flights departing exactly at 12:00 AM and 5:59 AM are included (time bucket boundary behavior).
Apply an arrival time bucket that ends at 11:59 PM and verify that flights arriving exactly at 11:59 PM are included.
Search with the minimum number of passengers supported (1 adult) and verify correct behavior.

Search with the maximum number of passengers supported by the UI (e.g., maximum adults/children/infants allowed in the passenger selector) and verify that search and filters still perform within the specified performance limits.
Perform searches during peak holiday traffic (simulated high load) and verify that initial results are still returned within 3 seconds and filter updates within 500 ms.

Switch between trip types (Round-trip, One-way, Multi-city) at the boundary of input validity (e.g., removing return date when switching from Round-trip to One-way) and verify that the system correctly resets or preserves only valid fields.

Use origin and destination that are geographically distant (e.g., intercontinental route like MAA to London) and verify that long-duration flights near the maximum duration boundary are handled correctly by the duration filter.

use_cases.use_case_title: Multi-city and passenger/class configuration flight search
use_cases.goal: Verify that users can configure multi-city journeys and different passenger and cabin class combinations, and that the system returns accurate, localized results with correct handling of edge cases.
preconditions: User can access Booking.com Flights page via web.
Multi-city search option is available on the Flights tab.
System supports Economy, Premium Economy, Business, and First class.
System supports adult, child, and infant passengers.
steps: Navigate to Booking.com and select the Flights tab.
Select trip type as Multi-city.
For leg 1, enter origin as MAA and destination as LHR with a valid future departure date.
For leg 2, enter origin as LHR and destination as MAA with a valid future departure date after leg 1.
Set passengers to a valid combination (e.g., 2 adults, 1 child, 1 infant).
Select cabin class as Economy.
Click Search and wait for results.
Verify that results are returned for the multi-city itinerary and that prices are shown in INR.
Change cabin class to Business and repeat the search.
Change passenger mix to 1 adult and repeat the search.
Observe that searches complete within the specified performance limits and that availability and pricing are consistent across legs.
expected_results: The system accepts multi-city input with at least two legs and valid dates and returns flight options for each leg.
Results for multi-city searches are displayed with pricing and availability for the entire itinerary, localized in INR.
Changing cabin class (e.g., from Economy to Business) results in updated pricing and availability appropriate for the selected class.
Changing passenger mix (e.g., from family to single adult) results in updated pricing and availability that reflect the new passenger configuration.
Initial results for each multi-city search are returned within 3 seconds.
The system maintains 99.9% availability and handles multi-city searches without errors under normal conditions.
Language and currency localization are applied consistently across all legs and result items.
negative_cases: Configure a multi-city search where the second leg's departure date is earlier than the first leg's departure date and verify that the system prevents the search or shows a clear error.
Configure a multi-city search with missing mandatory fields (e.g., no destination for one leg) and verify that the system does not proceed to results and highlights the missing information.
Attempt to add more legs than the UI allows for multi-city and verify that the system prevents adding additional legs beyond the limit.
Set an invalid passenger configuration if the UI allows (e.g., only infants without adults) and verify that the system prevents the search or shows an appropriate error.
Simulate no flights available for one or more legs of the multi-city itinerary and verify that the system clearly indicates unavailability without crashing.
Simulate an airline API timeout for one leg of the multi-city search and verify that the system handles it gracefully (e.g., partial results or clear error) without blocking the entire UI.
Attempt to perform a multi-city search with mixed invalid airport codes (e.g., valid origin and invalid destination) and verify that the system does not proceed and provides clear feedback.

Change cabin class to a class that is not available on a particular route (if such a case is returned by providers) and verify that the system handles it gracefully (e.g., no results for that class) rather than showing inconsistent data.
boundary_cases: Create a multi-city itinerary with the minimum number of legs allowed (e.g., 2 legs) and verify correct behavior.
Create a multi-city itinerary with the maximum number of legs allowed by the UI and verify that search performance and result rendering remain within specified limits.
Use the earliest allowed departure date for the first leg and the latest allowed date for the last leg and verify that the system accepts the range and returns results if available.
Use the minimum passenger count (1 adult) and maximum passenger count supported by the UI for multi-city searches and verify that the system handles both extremes correctly.
Select Economy for one search and First class for another and compare that the system correctly differentiates pricing and availability at the boundaries of cabin class options.
Perform multi-city searches during simulated peak holiday traffic and verify that initial results are still returned within 3 seconds and that the system remains responsive.

Use origin and destination combinations that are at the extremes of supported global routes (e.g., very long-haul legs) and verify that the system still returns valid options or clearly indicates if none are available.

assumptions: The Flights tab UI and behavior are consistent with the PRD descriptions and screenshots.
The date picker enforces some basic validation, but explicit behavior for invalid ranges is not fully specified and must be verified.
The maximum and minimum values for duration, passenger counts, and number of multi-city legs are not specified and must be discovered or clarified.
Behavior for invalid inputs (e.g., invalid airport codes, impossible passenger mixes) is not fully defined and must be validated or clarified.
The screenshots represent the current or target behavior of the production system for flight search and filters.
missing_info: Exact validation rules and error messages for invalid date ranges (e.g., return date before departure date).
Exact limits on number of passengers (adults, children, infants) and rules for allowed combinations.
Exact limits on the number of legs supported in a multi-city search.
Exact minimum and maximum values and step increments for the maximum travel time (duration) filter.
Detailed behavior and UI messaging when airline APIs time out or partially fail.
Exact behavior when filters result in zero results (wording and design of the 'no results' state).
Exact behavior when airline data (e.g., airline name) is missing for some fares.
Supported set of languages and currencies for localization and how fallback is handled.
Whether invalid airport codes can be entered directly or are fully prevented by an autocomplete-only UI.
